rationale: Round 0 built and ran correctly with no ICE, so the weights were shifted toward stronger obfuscation while keeping the cost/risk dimensions low so the selector avoids applying passes to AMGmk's hot numerical kernels (hypre_CSRMatrixMatvec/MatvecT, relax, GenerateSeqLaplacian). SUB gets the highest SecurityGain/DiversityGain since arithmetic obfuscation is cheap, safe, and effective on the integer index/pointer arithmetic that dominates CSR traversal code. IBR and BCF/FLA are raised moderately to obscure control flow in the large functions (hypre_CSRMatrixUnion, hypre_CSRMatrixMatvec), but their low RuntimeCost weights steer them away from inner SpMV loops where branch flattening and bogus predicates would hurt performance most. SPLIT stays mid-range as a low-risk size-tolerable diversifier of the biggest functions. ICALL is kept moderate: indirect calls complicate static call-graph recovery but carry indirect-branch overhead in tight loops. IGV remains the lowest since AMGmk has relatively few hot globals and global-variable rewriting carries the most correctness risk for numerical code; the elevated CorrectnessRisk weight further discourages its use on sensitive functions.
